text:
maria: kicking off a nightly CC-bench sweep for the candidate kernel set. aim: surface seqlen-dependent picks that diverge from prod kernels. filing quick notes here so we have an audit trail.

deploy-bot: nightly-sweep job started (job-id: ccbench-2026-04-01-179123) :gear: 

jon: nice. can you include seqlen buckets 16/64/256/1024? last time regressions showed only at 1024.

maria: yes. buckets are 16/64/256/1024. running with --batcher=continuous and --kv-mode=prefix-cache for this run. command: `./ccbench --kernels candidates.yaml --buckets 16,64,256,1024 --iters 1200 --batcher continuous --kv prefix`

kevin: heads-up: candidate-47 had a weird latency bump in the microprobe a week ago. might be related to kernel fallback path when seqlen > tile_size.

sasha: if it's a fallback to the reference matmul path, we should see increased L2 misses and higher stall cycles. include perf counters (LLC-loads, L2_RQSTS) in the run.

maria: added perf counters. also enabling trace sampling at step 32 for a few seeds. simple grep-able log output: ```
[ccbench] kernel=candidate-47, seq=1024, median_latency=18.4ms, p95=34.1ms
[ccbench] kernel=prod-opt,    seq=1024, median_latency=12.1ms, p95=13.8ms
[probe]    llc_miss_delta=+48% , l2_rqsts_delta=+22%
```

kevin: that's a pretty big delta. can you dump the kernel pick decision tree for that case? the runtime has a `seq_path` branch we can inspect.

maria: dumping small excerpt: ```
if seq <= 128: use kernel_a
elif seq <= 512: use kernel_b
else:
  if has_fp16_fastpath: use kernel_c
  else: use kernel_ref
```

jon: candidate-47 is kernel_c in that tree. maybe kernel_c's tile sizing is suboptimal on Ampere32? we saw similar on P100/RTX. we should add an arch-aware selector.

sasha: proposed quick fix: change selector to consider `seq % tile == 0` and `kv_stride` heuristics. sample rule: `prefer kernel_c if seq % 64 == 0 and kv_stride < 128`

maria: I'll enqueue a canary rerun that forces the selector change for just candidate-47 and seq=1024. label: `canary-seqlen-1024-k47`

deploy-bot: canary job queued (job-id: ccbench-canary-179123-canary-k47). ETA ~8m.

kevin: also add microprobe run with `--batch-size 1` to replicate single-request latency behavior. continuous batcher hides a lot of the kernel startup cost.

maria: done. added `--batch-size 1` matrix.

jon: if canary still fails, we should quarantine candidate-47 from the autotune pool and mark it as `needs-retune` in the kernel registry. then run the autotuner sweep to re-pick tile sizes and kernel params.

sasha: question: do we want the perf CI to fail the PR on p95 regressions > 20% for any seqlen bucket? our historical flakiness suggests 15% threshold is noisy.

maria: proposal: hard fail on >30% p95 regressions OR >20% median regressions; soft alert for 15-30% p95. soft alerts create a dashboard ticket but don't block PRs.

kevin: SGTM. add auto-attach of `perf-trace` tar to the CI artifact for any soft/hard regression so triage can repro locally.

maria: noted. I'll update the CI job: `--artifact-upload s3://redwood-perf/ccbench/${job-id}/` and add metadata tags `arch=ampere32, batcher=continuous, kv=prefix`.

jon: small implementation request: can we make the harness emit a `kernel_decision.jsonl` per run with fields: seq, kernel_chosen, reason, perf_counters? that'll speed triage.

maria: good idea. will add `--emit-decisions` flag. output will be newline-delimited JSON per sample.

sasha: ok let's wait for canary results. if it reproduces, I'll start a retune job with autotuner-v2 focusing on tile and unroll params.

deploy-bot: canary finished: job-id=ccbench-canary-179123-canary-k47, status=❌. artifact: s3://redwood-perf/ccbench/ccbench-canary-179123-canary-k47/trace.tar.gz

maria: canary confirms regression at seq=1024 p95:+180% vs prod-opt. attaching `kernel_decision.jsonl` and perf counters. linking the artifacts in the ticket.

kevin: moving candidate-47 -> quarantined in kernel-registry (reason: seqlen 1024 regression). tagging `needs-retune`.

jon: thanks. after retune, let's schedule a targeted micro-sweep across 768/896/1024 to test non-power-of-two boundaries. we often miss those.

maria: noted. creating follow-up ticket and a short runbook for oncall to interpret ccbench outputs. will paste runbook here when done. :memo:

sasha: thanks team. good catch from the nightly harness. this is exactly why the perf CI + ccbench matrix exists.

maria: closing thread for now, follow-ups in ticket PERF-4832.
